hypothesis: Separating catalogue construction from exact-cover search and replacing repeated dynamic compatibility-count scans with static rare-difference branching will expose materially more exact-cover search than the prior combined C++ run, while preserving the same exact DTS feasible set.
rationale: The prior native run reached a one-million-row catalogue but only depth 4 and 16521 search nodes during its combined wall budget. Its dynamic anchor selection rescans large inverted lists for every uncovered difference at every node. A persistent catalogue and static frequency order directly test whether that search-policy overhead, rather than lack of compatible rows, is the dominant barrier.
expected_information_gain: A substantially deeper finite search without a witness would isolate search-policy cost and quantify the remaining catalogue barrier; a verified scope<=111 assignment would be true-objective progress. A timeout remains finite evidence only.
method: Compile research_tools/search_dts_cpp_separated_exact_cover.cpp with the pinned WSL2 compiler. Phase A generates up to 1,000,000 deduplicated valid scope<=111 Golomb-ruler masks from seeded uniform sampling and persists a binary catalogue. Phase B reads that exact catalogue, builds the inverted difference index, orders uncovered differences by static catalogue frequency, branches on the first currently uncovered difference with at least one compatible row, allows at most six explicit gaps, and ranks candidates by inverse-frequency rarity. Independently validate any complete seven-row assignment with the repository integer verifier.
metric: catalogue size, generation attempts, search nodes, maximum depth, gap count, elapsed phase times, returned rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: Only a complete seven-row assignment accepted by the independent integer verifier is a scope<=111 true-objective witness; catalogue size, depth, and timeout are finite methodological evidence.

configuration.catalog_format: versioned binary rows with marks and masks
configuration.row_generator: seeded uniform sorted 5-mark samples with internal Golomb check
configuration.branching: static rarest currently uncovered difference with six-gap budget

compute_budget.cpu: single native C++ process per phase
compute_budget.memory_intent: persistent compact row catalogue and bounded inverted indexes

kill_condition: Stop generation at catalogue target, 10,000,000 attempts, or 120 seconds; stop search at first complete assignment, 240 seconds, 100,000,000 nodes, or precise runtime failure. Independently validate any returned assignment. Do not infer infeasibility from a finite catalogue or timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: methodological improvement is deeper search; strict objective improvement requires independent validation of scope<=111

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: phase separation and static branching should increase search throughput without changing the feasible set

interpretation: Separating catalogue construction reduced generation to 4.37 seconds, but static rare-difference branching still exhausted the 240-second search budget at depth 5 and only 1796 nodes. The hypothesis that dynamic compatibility-count scans were the dominant barrier is falsified for this catalogue/search family; no DTS witness was returned.
what_was_learned: The one-million-row catalogue is readily constructible, but the exact-cover tree is dominated by candidate branching or row scarcity rather than catalogue construction. The prior dynamic anchor-count policy reached depth 4; the separated static policy reached depth 5 but did not make the target computationally accessible. Further random-catalogue tuning has low expected value.
recommended_next_action: Close this random-catalogue exact-cover family. Resume DTS only with a materially different decomposition such as on-demand constraint-generated rows or a justified structural construction; otherwise keep DTS paused.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the prior combined C++ run: it persists the catalogue between phases and changes the branch-selection policy from exact dynamic compatibility minimization to a static rare-difference policy, directly testing the diagnosed bottleneck.
